items.title: 68145_Jimmie Rowles oral history interview
items.q: I wrote a whole lot of stuff for that band. The funny part about it is that Lee insisted that we memorize the music, and nobody used it.

ctx.x: As far as the musical policy was concerned, did Lee handle that, too, or was that Lester's...?

That was sort of everybody. Nobody really... I wrote a whole lot of stuff for that band. The funny part about it is that Lee insisted that we memorize the music, and nobody used it. So I wrote out a chorus on "Body And Soul," and Lester could never remember his part -- because he was in the middle; you know, he wasn't playing the lead. And he used to say, "Wait a minute, wait a minute," and he reached in his back pocket and he pulled this thing out, folded up, and he'd fold it over the edge of the piano, and he'd…
Did he ever talk about why he left Basie?

items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: But at this time, Jimmy Rowles was playing piano with me then.

ctx.x: That's right, and this is where Lady Day worked with us. Oh yeah, oh yeah -- she worked there for several weeks. Billy Holiday. But at this time, Jimmy Rowles was playing piano with me then. Okay. So when Jimmy Rowles first came to town, he worked with Lee Lester Young's band, and Bumps and Red and Louis Gonzales.

So we worked at the Trouville for awhile, and -- that was a real good job. We didn't go to work until 10 o'clock at night. We played at 10, and we -- you know, off at 10:30 and go back at 11, you know, go back on at 12, go back on at 1, and stay until 1:30, and that was the end of our gig.
